threads.title: The Beloved commanded to descend through all the heavens
threads.summary_md: Isaiah hears the Most High send His Beloved down into the world He made: *"And I heard the voice of the Most High, the Father of my Lord, saying to my Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) who will be called Yahusha (Jesus)"* and *"Go forth and descend through all the heavens, and thou wilt descend to the firmament and that world: to the angel in Sheol thou wilt descend, but to Haguel thou wilt not go"* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:7-8). It ain't new — Paul sings the same descent: the One in the form of Elohim *made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant* (Philippians 2:7), and John names Him as the only one who *came down from heaven* (John 3:13). The pre-Christian prophet already saw the kenosis.

members.note: Philippians 2:6 — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* The Beloved the Father commissions in Ascension of Isaiah 10:7 is the very One Paul says was in the form of Elohim before His descent.

Philippians 2:7 — *But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:* The command to go forth and descend through all the heavens (Ascension of Isaiah 10:8) is exactly this self-emptying into the lower world.

John 3:13 — *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* The descent to the firmament and Sheol in Ascension of Isaiah 10:8 is the same one who alone came down from heaven.

1 Timothy 3:16 — *And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: Elohim (God) was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.* The mystery Paul names as the gospel is the very descent and ascent Isaiah is shown in Ascension of Isaiah 10:8.

threads.title: Unknown to the heavens, sent to judge the gods of this world
threads.summary_md: The Beloved descends hidden, that *"none of the angels of that world shall know that Thou art with Me"* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:11), until He judges *"and destroy the princes and angels and gods of that world"* (10:12) — *"For they have denied Me and said: 'We alone are and there is none beside us'"* (10:13). The rulers' boast is the old idolatrous lie the prophets unmasked; the descent comes to spoil them. Paul names the same hidden victory: the descended One *led captivity captive* (Ephesians 4:8), and the suffering Just One went *and preached unto the spirits in prison* (1 Peter 3:19). It ain't new.

members.note: Ephesians 4:8 — *Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.* The descent to judge and destroy the princes of that world (Ascension of Isaiah 10:12) is the captivity led captive when the Beloved ascends again.

1 Peter 3:19 — *By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;* The Beloved sent to judge the angels and gods of that world (Ascension of Isaiah 10:12) is the One who descended to the imprisoned spirits.

Isaiah 6:5 — *Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* The princes' boast *We alone are and there is none beside us* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:13) is the inversion of the throne-vision the same prophet records, where Yahuah alone is King.

threads.title: He ascends in glory and sits on the right hand
threads.summary_md: After the descent the Father promises the return: *"And afterwards from the angels of death Thou wilt ascend to Thy place. And Thou wilt not be transformed in each heaven, but in glory wilt Thou ascend and sit on My right hand"* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:14) — *"And thereupon the princes and powers of that world will worship Thee"* (10:15). It ain't new — this is the enthronement Hebrews proclaims: He *sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high* (Hebrews 1:3), and Philippians' answering hymn, that *every knee should bow* (Philippians 2:10). The descent and the exaltation are one arc, seen centuries before the cross.

members.note: Hebrews 1:3 — *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* The promise that the Beloved will *ascend and sit on My right hand* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:14) is the very enthronement Hebrews announces.

Philippians 2:10 — *That at the name of Yahusha (Jesus) every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;* The princes and powers worshipping the ascended Beloved (Ascension of Isaiah 10:15) is the universal homage Paul foretells.

Revelation 5:12 — *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* The worship the powers render the exalted One (Ascension of Isaiah 10:15) is the heavenly acclamation John hears before the throne.

threads.title: The praise of the seven heavens before the Great Glory
threads.summary_md: Isaiah, carried up, hears *"the voices and the giving of praise, which I had heard in each of the six heavens, ascending and being heard there"* and beholds *"that Glorious One whose glory I could not behold"* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:1-2), with *"Yahuah (Lord) and the angel of the Spirit"* attending all (10:4). The prophet who once saw Yahuah *high and lifted up* in the temple now sees the same throne above the heavens. It ain't new — Isaiah 6's *Holy, holy, holy* (Isaiah 6:3) becomes Revelation's ten thousand times ten thousand round about the throne (Revelation 5:11). One worship, one Glory, across the testaments.

members.note: Isaiah 6:3 — *And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): the whole earth is full of his glory.* The Glory Isaiah cannot behold in Ascension of Isaiah 10:2 is the same thrice-holy Yahuah he saw in the temple vision.

Revelation 5:11 — *And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;* The praise ascending through the six heavens (Ascension of Isaiah 10:1) is the same throng John hears encircling the throne.

Revelation 5:14 — *And the four beasts said, Amen. And the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him that liveth for ever and ever.* Yahuah and the angel of the Spirit beholding all the praise in Ascension of Isaiah 10:4 is the worship before the eternal throne John records.

threads.title: Descending unrecognized, made like the angels of each realm
threads.summary_md: Isaiah watches the Lord go down heaven by heaven, *"made Himself like unto the form of the angels there"* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:20), giving the password at each gate *"in order that He should not be recognized"* (10:24), down to the firmament where *"dwelleth the ruler of this world"* (10:29). It ain't new — Paul asks, *what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?* (Ephesians 4:9), and John says *the world was made by him, and the world knew him not* (John 1:10). The hidden descent of the incarnate Word, foreseen.

members.note: Ephesians 4:9 — *(Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?* The descent to the firmament where the ruler of this world dwells (Ascension of Isaiah 10:29) is Paul's descent into the lower parts of the earth.

John 1:10 — *He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.* The Lord made like the angels so as not to be recognized (Ascension of Isaiah 10:20) is the Word coming unknown to the world He made.

John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The Lord taking the form of the lower angels (Ascension of Isaiah 10:20) is the Word made flesh and dwelling among us.
